question: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, a renowned musician from India is known for playing which of the following instruments?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarod**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Amjad Ali Khan**

 
 
• **Ustad Amjad Ali Khan** born on 9th October 1945 is an **Indian classical sarod player**, best known for his clear and fast ekhara taans.
 
• Ustad Amjad Khan was honored with **Padma Shri** in **1975**, **Padma Bhushan** in **1991**, and **Padma Vibhushan** in **2001**.
 
• Ustad Amjad Khan was also awarded **21st Rajiv Gandhi National Sadbhavna Award**, the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in **1989**, and the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship** in **2011**.
 
• **Sarod**: It is a stringed instrument.
 
• Sarod known for its deep, weighty, introspective sound, widely used in folk music.
 
• The U.S. state of Massachusetts proclaimed **20 April** as **Amjad Ali Khan Day** in **1984**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** sarod**

 
 
• The **sarod** is a stringed instrument, used in Hindustani music on the Indian subcontinent. Along with the sitar, it is among the most popular and prominent instruments.
 
• The** Jal Tarang** is a melodic percussion instrument that originates from the Indian subcontinent. It consists of a set of ceramic or metal bowls filled with water. The bowls are played by striking the edge with beaters, one in each hand.
 
 
 
• **Sarangi**
 
 
• The **sarangi** is a bowed, short-necked string instrument played in traditional music from India – Punjabi folk music, Rajasthani folk music, and Boro folk music – also in Pakistan and Bangladesh.
 
 
 
• **Veena**
 
 
• The V**eena** also spelled vina, comprises various chordophone instruments from the Indian subcontinent. Ancient musical instruments evolved into many variations, such as lutes, zithers, and arched harps.
